subject: general
question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 18 days, respectively. Both work for 2 days and then A goes away and B completed the remaining work alone. The whole work was completed in ______________ days.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 12, 18) = 36 units.

Efficiency: A = 3, B = 2.

Combined work for 2 days = (3 + 2) × 2 = 10 units.

Remaining work = 36 − 10 = 26 units.

Time taken by B for remaining work = 26 ÷ 2 = 13 days.

Total time = 2 + 13 = 15 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 12 days, Time taken by **B** = 18 days. Both work for 2 days.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 **A** 12 36 3 
 **B** 18 2 

⇒ **Total Work** = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units

⇒ **Efficiency** of A = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units/day

⇒ **Efficiency** of B = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 units/day

⇒ Work done by **A and B** in 2 days = (3 + 2) × 2 = 10 units

⇒ **Remaining Work** = 36 − 10 = 26 units

⇒ Time taken by **B alone** to finish remaining work = 26 ÷ 2 = 13 days

⇒ **Total time** taken to complete the work = 2 + 13 = 15 days

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Total work is usually considered as the **LCM** of the time taken by individuals to simplify efficiency calculations.

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

Leaving Work Logic

If a person leaves, subtract the work done before leaving from the **total work** and divide the remaining work by the efficiency of the remaining person.</p
